# Tabitha Pratt

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** unmarried  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>
- **Origin:** the Glen  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052)</sub>
- **Role:** general servant  <sub>[v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Tabitha Pratt is an aged, gray, and stern-visaged woman. She is described as scrawny and austere in appearance, though possessing a kindly presence.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c24 P0](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0000), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c30 P14](../source/v05-c30.md#nw-v05-c30-p0014)_

## Personality

Tabitha is fiercely loyal, sensible, and deeply devoted to the Carrow family, ruling Hollowmere with absolute authority as a protective servant. She is candid, pragmatic, and unbothered by supernatural fears, often facing troubling situations with calm determination or a pitchfork. Though she holds severe views on discipline and morality, she possesses a warm heart and loves gossip and local affairs. She harbors a lifelong, humorous regret that no man ever courted or proposed to her.

_Sources: [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 c24 P0](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0000), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c1 P7](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0007), [v5 c1 P9](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0009), [v5 c1 P10](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0010), [v5 c15 P3](../source/v05-c15.md#nw-v05-c15-p0003), [v5 c30 P14](../source/v05-c30.md#nw-v05-c30-p0014), [v5 c30 P22](../source/v05-c30.md#nw-v05-c30-p0022), [v5 c30 P23](../source/v05-c30.md#nw-v05-c30-p0023)_

## History

Tabitha Pratt began working as a general servant for Nell Carrow at the small house of dreams. Despite initial suspicion from Thirza Abernethy, Tabitha quickly formed a deep, devoted affection for Nell, whom she affectionately called 'young Mrs. Doctor'. She faithfully managed the household during Nell's illness after the loss of her first baby and stayed on through subsequent seasons. When Dr. Carrow purchased the Varley property at Hollowmere, Tabitha moved with the family, delighted to be closer to society in the Glen. She helped raise all of Nell's children, forming an exceptionally strong maternal bond with young Harcourt during Nell's prolonged illness following his birth. At Hollowmere, Tabitha remained the commanding authority of the household, keeping up with local Glen gossip, attending Presbytarian church affairs, and fearlessly protecting the home.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P0](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0000), [v4 c19 P7](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0007), [v4 c19 P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010), [v4 c22 P0](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0000), [v4 c40 P41](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0041), [v4 c40 P42](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0042), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c1 P4](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0004), [v5 c1 P7](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0007)_

## Quotes

> Time for breakfast now. It is my belief that some food and drink will be welcomed by us all. Instruct young Mrs. Doctor to be entirely free of concern—Tabitha is taking charge. Instruct her to occupy her thoughts solely with her infant.  <sub>[v4 c19 P10](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0010)</sub>

> An old maid I may be, yet you do not catch ME speaking ill of men. They suit me fine. Had the opportunity arisen, I would gladly have wed one.  <sub>[v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005)</sub>

> Mrs. Dr. dear, I brought him into this world every bit as much as you. The baby belongs to me every bit as much as he belongs to you.  <sub>[v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005)</sub>

> Writing poetry has never brought about any benefit in my experience, and I trust and petition that that precious boy will leave the inclination behind. Should he fail to do so—it remains for us to observe what a cod-liver oil emulsion can accomplish.  <sub>[v5 c7 P48](../source/v05-c07.md#nw-v05-c07-p0048)</sub>

> Mrs. Dr. dear, I do not question that her decision is quite practical, yet personally I have constantly held the opinion that should I ever get wed, I would choose the veil and white to feel more like a bride.  <sub>[v5 c35 P3](../source/v05-c35.md#nw-v05-c35-p0003)</sub>
